LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what has been read, • discuss the topics of the texts with peers, 1. How does reading widely help us learn better?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text for information and enjoyment
2. appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a text for information and enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to read a text for information and enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a text for information and enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a text for information and enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a text for information and enjoyment)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a text for information and enjoyment.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what has been read, • discuss the topics of the texts with peers, 1. How does reading widely help us learn better?
2. What should one consider when choosing a reading text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a text for information and enjoyment.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of extensive reading in lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
